mission_09: Forecast evaluation is critical for selecting the best model, tuning hyperparameters, and communicating prediction quality to stakeholders. Different metrics capture different aspects of forecast accuracy and are appropriate for different use cases. Mean Absolute Error (MAE) provides an interpretable measure of average error magnitude in the original units. Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) penalizes large errors more heavily, making it sensitive to outliers. Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) expresses error as a percentage, enabling comparison across series with different scales, but it is undefined for zero values and asymmetric. Symmetric MAPE (SMAPE) addresses the asymmetry by using the average of actual and predicted values in the denominator. Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE) scales errors by the in-sample naive forecast error, providing a scale-free metric that works even with intermittent demand. The Diebold-Mariano test formally compares two forecasts by testing whether their loss differential has a mean significantly different from zero, accounting for serial correlation in the loss differential. In this mission, you will implement a comprehensive suite of evaluation metrics and statistical tests for comparing forecasting models.
